idea: Halftone photo of a brass marine chronometer in its gimbaled box (Smithsonian open access style archive scan), caption: 'The hard part of the ocean was knowing what time it was.' For people who like the idea that longitude was a clockmaking problem.

A halftone sextant on a plain table, caption: 'Angle between two things you can see. Position of the one thing you can't.' A quiet, smart shirt for anyone who loves how navigation reasons from small measurements.

Photograph of a worn 19th-century pocket compass, open, needle blurred, caption: 'Still points to the same place. Has been wrong about it for centuries.' A nod to magnetic north wandering and declination.
Halftone of a plaster relief model of an alpine massif (archival survey-office photo), caption: 'The mountain, but you can lose it in a drawer.' Appeals to map nerds who love terrain made small.
A large antique terrestrial globe in a library, photographed at an angle, caption: 'Everything we knew, and a sea serpent where we didn't.' Funny, literate, and honest about the edges of knowledge.

Survey crew carrying a theodolite on a tripod across a salt flat or dry plain (Library of Congress / USGS archive), caption: 'Somebody had to walk it first.' Tribute to the unglamorous people who measured the map into being.
Halftone of a surveyor's chain (Gunter's chain) coiled on a boulder, caption: 'One chain. Sixty-six feet. Eighty of them make a mile.' For people who enjoy odd, exact old units.
Photo of a USGS benchmark disc set in rock, caption: 'You are exactly here. Give or take a millimeter, officially.' A point-of-view shirt about being located, with a wry bureaucratic tone.
Archival photo of a lighthouse Fresnel lens, a halo of glass rings, caption: 'A very organized way to say: not that way.' Beautiful object, dry joke about navigation as warning.
Halftone of an astrolabe photographed head-on, caption: 'A phone for the sky, 1,200 years early.' Appeals to history-of-science fans and gives them an instant conversation.
A sounding-lead line being swung from a survey ship's bow (NOAA historical photo library), caption: 'Depth, one splash at a time.' For people who like mapping what can't be seen.
Photo of a Mercator-projection wall map being unrolled by two clerks, caption: 'Greenland is not that big. We checked.' Shirt for the geography pedant who loves projection arguments.
NASA-style archival photograph of an Apollo-era star tracker or sextant instrument panel, caption: 'Even the rockets kept a sextant for emergencies.' Surprising fact, beautiful hardware.
Halftone of a ship's logbook open beside a pair of brass dividers, caption: 'Day 41. Nothing but water and arithmetic.' Evocative, bookish, and a little funny.

Pack mules carrying a boundary-survey party up a canyon in the 1900s (Smithsonian or LoC), caption: 'The border was drawn here, by hand, uphill.' For anyone who appreciates that lines on maps cost somebody a lot of walking.
Aerial survey camera mounted in the belly of a biplane, 1920s, caption: 'The first time anyone saw the whole county.' A shirt about perspective and the moment maps became pictures.
A weathered surveyor's cairn on a bare summit with a tripod beacon, caption: 'Left so the next person would know where we were.' Gentle, thoughtful, and about leaving a mark that is useful.
Photo of a hand-cranked wind-up odometer wheel on a dirt road (a perambulator), caption: 'Distance, honestly measured.' Minimal, odd and charming for people who like measuring things the slow way.
Halftone of a ship's pelorus or azimuth compass on a bridge wing, caption: 'North is a suggestion. Magnetic, true, grid: pick one.' For those who like the awkward truth that there are three norths.

Archival photo of a cartographer's drafting table with pens, scribers and a half-finished coastline, caption: 'The coast was a guess until it wasn't.' Respect for the draftspeople who finished the map by hand.
